```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", error = FALSE, cache = FALSE)
library(llmsa)
numeric_validation <- new.env(parent = globalenv())
sys.source(system.file("validation", "numeric", "reference_checks.R",
                       package = "llmsa", mustWork = TRUE), envir = numeric_validation)
context <- numeric_validation$validation_context()
anchors <- numeric_validation$validation_anchors(context)
checks <- numeric_validation$validation_run(context)
```

## Variance components and gauge R&R (numeric)

These calculations compare the numeric random-effects model with independent
ANOVA calculations, published estimates, certified NIST quantities and live
package oracles. Every observed value is recomputed by the currently loaded
`llmsa` namespace. No fitted estimates or oracle results are stored as inputs.
The reference calculations are implemented in the installed
`validation/numeric/reference_checks.R` script.

The reference authority is `reference/anchors/`: ANK-10 contains the AIAG
example, ANK-13 the published Penicillin estimates, ANK-14 the NIST certified
quantities, ANK-16 the GRR conventions, and ANK-TOL the comparison tolerances.
Variance-component tolerances are fractions of the reference **total**
variance; derived ratios use relative tolerances. Printed standard deviations
are compared on the variance scale where the anchor requires it. The tables
show the resulting absolute bounds.

This run uses the **`r checks$context`** context. A nonempty `REPO_ROOT`
selects complete local validation: original anchors, the protected AIAG sheet
and the frozen NIST originals. Missing inputs or mismatching SHA-256 hashes
stop the calculation. Without `REPO_ROOT`, the public package build uses whole,
byte-identical anchor copies and free NIST tables. Their provenance is recorded
in `validation/numeric/SOURCES.json`. In that context, AIAG rows explicitly say
`not rerun: protected data required` and never claim a successful rerun.
Neither context displays the protected AIAG measurements.

The balanced synthetic studies use the specification's four crossed designs
with seed one, with and without block effects and pairwise interactions.
The independent ANOVA calculation solves the expected-mean-square equations;
negative moment estimates are outside that comparison. At a variance boundary,
the numeric default fit re-estimates the remaining components by restricted
REML. The AIAG comparison pools the interaction as in the handbook; that row
is marked as not separately estimated. The model with interaction is reported
separately. On the unbalanced `ic50_demo` data,
`VCA::remlVCA` is a criterion, while `VCA::anovaVCA` is a reported comparison.
`SixSigma::ss.rr` uses its default interaction pooling; study variation comes
from its unrounded standard deviations.

```{r reference-tables, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
for (name in names(checks$tables)) {
  cat("\n### ", name, "\n\n", sep = "")
  print(knitr::kable(checks$tables[[name]], row.names = FALSE))
  cat("\n\n")
}
```

### NIST precision report

Item denotes the treatment and replicate denotes the observation within the
treatment. The certified within mean square is the residual variance;
the item reference is the between-minus-within mean-square difference divided
by the number of replicates. NIST labels `AtmWtAg` as **Average** difficulty;
the project nevertheless applies the stricter relative tolerance
`r numeric_validation$validation_tolerance(anchors, "nist_digits", "low_difficulty_rel_tol")`
to it, as to the lower-difficulty datasets.

Log relative error (LRE) is the negative base-ten logarithm of the absolute
relative error. Exact agreement gives `Inf`. For `SmLs04` through `SmLs06`,
the required LRE is at least the corresponding `stats::aov` LRE minus
`r numeric_validation$validation_lre_margin(anchors)`. The higher-difficulty
`SmLs07` through `SmLs09` are reports, with no pass threshold. Low LRE values
expose precision loss, including loss in the original-scale lme4 model despite
conditioning the variance-ratio calculation. `NA` denotes a failed fit whose
reason is reported below; rounded input values are never repaired.

```{r nist-lre, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
print(knitr::kable(checks$lre, digits = 6, row.names = FALSE))
```

```{r fit-diagnostics, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
if (nrow(checks$diagnostics)) {
  cat("\nFit diagnostics:\n\n")
  print(knitr::kable(checks$diagnostics, row.names = FALSE))
} else {
  cat("\nNo fit warnings or errors were recorded in this run.\n")
}
```

### Reproduction and interpretation

Run `Rscript data-raw/make_validation_numeric.R` from the repository to
reproduce the public inputs offline. The script checks original hashes before
writing; `--out <package-root>` reproduces the files in a separate directory.
The local NIST collection belongs in the sibling `quellen/daten/` directory,
and the protected AIAG sheet at the path recorded in ANK-10. The installed
`validation/numeric/README.md` explains both build contexts and their checks.

The default numeric fit uses a closed EMS solution for eligible balanced
designs and an analytic REML completion otherwise. Supplying any lme4 argument
through `...` selects the direct lme4 path; the ANOVA reference check uses the
optimizer declared by ANK-TOL. The final model retains the original response
scale, observation order and factor labels. Its components come from
`VarCorr()`. Bootstrap refits use ordinary lme4 optimization with the stored
refit control; the initial analytic completion is not repeated per replicate.

Zero total variance makes percentages, ICC and ndc undefined (`NA`), with
verdict `undetermined`. Zero gauge variance with positive item variance gives
infinite ndc; zero item variance with positive gauge variance gives the lower
bound from ANK-16. Constant numeric responses and a degenerate residual
variance produce named errors. These finite reference checks establish neither
bootstrap coverage nor the later ordinal and binary simulation results.

## Ordinal and binary outcomes (latent scale)

```{r latent-setup, include=FALSE}
latent_validation <- new.env(parent = globalenv())
sys.source(system.file("validation", "latent", "reference_checks.R",
                       package = "llmsa", mustWork = TRUE), envir = latent_validation)
latent_context <- latent_validation$latent_context()
latent_anchors <- latent_validation$latent_anchors(latent_context)
latent_checks <- latent_validation$latent_reference_checks(latent_anchors)
latent_results <- setNames(lapply(latent_validation$latent_studies,
                                latent_validation$latent_read_results),
                           latent_validation$latent_studies)
m1d_validation <- new.env(parent = globalenv())
sys.source(system.file("validation", "m1d", "findings.R", package = "llmsa", mustWork = TRUE),
           envir = m1d_validation)
m1d_anchors <- m1d_validation$m1d_resources()
```

Ordinal `msa_fit()` uses cumulative link mixed models and binary `msa_fit()`
uses binomial mixed models. Variance components, gauge R&R and `ICC_items`
refer to the latent scale. ANK-28 fixes the residual variance to one for the
probit link and to `pi^2 / 3` for the logit link. In both cases, `ICC_items` is
the item variance divided by the sum of all variance components, including
that residual. Gauge R&R includes every component except the item variance.

All reference values below are read from ANK-21, ANK-25 and ANK-28, with
tolerances from ANK-TOL. The **`r latent_context$mode`** context verifies
whole anchor copies and their SHA-256 manifest under `validation/latent/`.
When `REPO_ROOT` is set, original anchors are also checked and used; an
invalid root or missing input is an error. There is no network access.

### Wine: ordinal components and a separate installation check

The wine comparison maps bottle to item, judge to prompt, with one model and
one replicate. Each link is fitted again with `ordinal::clmm` and `msa_fit()`.
The absolute comparison bound is `ANK-TOL.engine_ordinal` times the direct
fit's total latent variance. The tutorial's `clmm2` model includes temperature
and contact fixed effects, so its ANK-21 estimates form a separate installation
check, using both Laplace approximation and quadrature.

```{r latent-wine, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
print(knitr::kable(latent_validation$latent_display(latent_checks$wine), row.names = FALSE))
cat("\n\n")
print(knitr::kable(latent_validation$latent_display(latent_checks$ordinal_installation), row.names = FALSE))
```

### BeetlesMale: binary repeatability and a separate installation check

Population is the item, with one prompt, one model and replicates numbered
within Population. The latent logit `ICC_items` is compared with live
`rptR::rptBinary(expect = "liability")`, `performance::icc()` on both the
direct `glmer` model and the returned model, and the independent calculation
`variance(Population) / (variance(Population) + pi^2 / 3)` using ANK-28.
These comparisons use `ANK-TOL.rptr.live_tol`.

The published ANK-25 values use rptR's default `expect = "meanobs"` and a
different scale convention. Both the link and original scale values are
reproduced separately with `ANK-TOL.rptr.vignette_tol`. They are installation
checks, not reference values for `ICC_items`.

```{r latent-beetles, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
print(knitr::kable(latent_validation$latent_display(latent_checks$binary), row.names = FALSE))
cat("\n\n")
print(knitr::kable(latent_validation$latent_display(latent_checks$rptr_installation), row.names = FALSE))
if (length(latent_checks$diagnostics)) {
  cat("\n\nRecorded fit diagnostics:\n\n")
  print(knitr::kable(data.frame(Diagnostic = latent_checks$diagnostics), row.names = FALSE))
}
```

### Simulation recovery and two-level factors

The following tables read the installed studies' `<study>_results.csv` if it
exists, otherwise `<study>_check_results.csv`. An invalid existing full result
file stops the build. The displayed `n_sim` comes from each file. Knitting
does not run simulations. Bias, relative bias, empirical standard error
(EmpSE) and root mean squared error (RMSE) each have a Monte Carlo standard
error (MCSE); the tables retain significant digits for small estimates.
`n_finite` and `n_failed` count the usable and missing estimates separately.
Finite estimates with non-convergence or singularity are retained, with the
diagnoses recorded in the replicate and session files.

Short runs check reproducibility and file structure. They do not establish
quantitative recovery or bias findings. Full runs require at least
`r latent_validation$latent_get(latent_anchors, "ANK-06", "value", "n_sim_min")`
repetitions per scenario, according to ANK-06, and are performed separately
by the operator after acceptance. The installed `validation/sim/README.md`
gives executable full-run and scenario-merging instructions, the ADEMP design,
MCSE formulas and failure handling. The random stream for each scenario and
repetition is independent of the requested run length and worker count.

For ordinal fits, a prompt, model or block with exactly two levels enters as
a fixed effect. Its component is the squared fitted difference divided by
two, `beta-hat^2 / 2`, marked in `attr(fit$vc, "derived")` and in `msa_grr()`.
This range method does not subtract the AIAG correction `EV^2 / (n * r)`.
Its bias is positive: `E[beta-hat^2 / 2] = sigma^2 + Var(beta-hat) / 2`.
Every such fit warns, and printing names each derived component with
`range method, see ?msa_fit`. The `two_level` study redraws both model effects
in every repetition and reports `derived_share`, the fraction of repetitions
with a derived model component. The full-run tables below report its measured
bias and MCSE in each scenario. A bias that does not exceed the reporting
threshold does not establish general unbiasedness. Fewer than three ordinal
items are rejected.

Component findings use ANK-TOL.bias_report: the absolute relative bias must
exceed both `r m1d_anchors[["ANK-TOL"]]$value$bias_report$rel_bias` and
`r m1d_anchors[["ANK-TOL"]]$value$bias_report$mcse_multiple` times its MCSE.
The two-level model bias is always reported; its direction is resolved only
beyond `r m1d_anchors[["ANK-TOL"]]$value$mc_factor$report` MCSE. These are
reporting rules, not acceptance criteria for the estimates. Full-run findings
are computed from the read tables, never selected by scenario name.

```{r latent-simulation-tables, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
for (study in names(latent_results)) {
  entry <- latent_results[[study]]
  cat("\n### ", study, "\n\n", sep = "")
  cat("Read `", basename(entry$path), "` (", entry$mode, "); n_sim = ",
      entry$n_sim, " per scenario.\n\n", sep = "")
  for (scenario in unique(entry$data$scenario)) {
    cat("\n", scenario, "\n\n", sep = "")
    rows <- entry$data[entry$data$scenario == scenario, , drop = FALSE]
    performance <- rows[rows$measure != "derived_share", , drop = FALSE]
    print(knitr::kable(latent_validation$latent_display(performance), row.names = FALSE))
    if (any(rows$measure == "derived_share")) {
      cat("\n\nDerived-component diagnostic:\n\n")
      print(knitr::kable(latent_validation$latent_display(rows[rows$measure == "derived_share", , drop = FALSE]),
                         row.names = FALSE))
    }
    cat("\n\n")
  }
  if (entry$mode == "full") {
    findings <- m1d_validation$m1d_findings(study, entry$data, m1d_anchors)
    cat("\nReportable findings (values and MCSE on the stated measure's scale):\n\n")
    if (nrow(findings)) {
      print(knitr::kable(m1d_validation$m1d_display(findings, digits = 6L), row.names = FALSE))
    } else cat("No component exceeds the anchored report threshold.\n")
  } else cat("\nShort run: no full-run finding is claimed.\n")
  cat("\n\n")
}
```

### Ordinal convergence sensitivity

The main summaries above retain finite estimates even when a fit did not
converge. The following separate analysis compares all finite estimates with
only those whose recorded `converged` flag is true. Singular fits are retained
in both eligible groups. Each n comes from the replicate rows used by that
group, independently of the result table's n_sim. Non-convergence, singularity
and missing flags are counted separately per actual outer repetition.

Bias MCSE is EmpSE divided by the square root of n; relative bias and its
MCSE divide by the truth and its absolute value, respectively. EmpSE MCSE
uses the ADEMP approximation in the formula collection, section 9. Selecting
on convergence can itself introduce selection bias: this comparison is a
descriptive sensitivity analysis, not a replacement estimator or a reason
to discard inconvenient estimates from the main study.

```{r convergence-sensitivity, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
sensitivity <- m1d_validation$m1d_convergence_sensitivity()
if (sensitivity$available) {
  print(knitr::kable(m1d_validation$m1d_display(sensitivity$diagnostics, digits = 6L), row.names = FALSE,
                     caption = "Diagnostics over actual outer repetitions; unknown flags are shown separately."))
  for (scenario in sort(unique(sensitivity$tables$scenario))) {
    cat("\n\n", scenario, "\n\n", sep = "")
    rows <- sensitivity$tables[sensitivity$tables$scenario == scenario, , drop = FALSE]
    print(knitr::kable(m1d_validation$m1d_display(rows, digits = 6L), row.names = FALSE))
  }
} else cat(sensitivity$reason, ". The full-run acceptance still requires the replicate file.\n", sep = "")
```

## Bootstrap intervals: coverage by scenario

```{r coverage-setup, include=FALSE}
coverage_validation <- new.env(parent = globalenv())
sys.source(system.file("validation", "sim", "boot_coverage_results.R",
                       package = "llmsa", mustWork = TRUE), envir = coverage_validation)
coverage_results <- coverage_validation$boot_read_results()
```

This section reads **`r basename(coverage_results$path)`**
(**`r coverage_results$mode`** run), with
**n_sim = `r coverage_results$n_sim`** repetitions per scenario. The installed
`boot_coverage_results.csv` takes precedence over
`boot_coverage_check_results.csv`. An invalid existing full result stops the
build. Knitting reads the results and starts neither simulations nor downloads.

The study evaluates the existing 95% percentile intervals from `msa_boot()`
for gauge R&R study variation and contribution, ndc and item ICC. Every outer
repetition generates a new crossed study and uses the package's default number
of parametric bootstrap refits. Numeric scenarios include all three pairwise
interactions; the binary logit scenario uses item, prompt and model effects.
The installed `validation/sim/README.md` specifies the designs, seeds,
Monte Carlo standard errors (MCSE), diagnostics and reproduction commands.

Coverage is the fraction of finite closed intervals containing the true value;
width is their mean width. Their `n_finite` and `n_failed` count available and
unavailable outer repetitions. For bootstrap diagnostics, the unit of analysis
is also the outer repetition: each contributes its fraction of singular or
failed refits, and MCSE is the standard error of the mean of those fractions.
Singular refits with finite statistics remain in the intervals. Only
non-finite values are omitted, separately for each statistic. The diagnostics
count a replicate with any non-finite statistic as failed and do not also
count it as singular.

Short runs establish reproducibility and file structure. They do not establish
nominal coverage. Full runs require at least
`r coverage_results$n_min` repetitions per scenario
(ANK-06) and follow code acceptance. Undercoverage or overcoverage in those
runs is a finding to report, with MCSE, rather than a reason to alter intervals.
The reporting threshold is ANK-TOL.mc_factor.report, or
`r m1d_anchors[["ANK-TOL"]]$value$mc_factor$report` MCSE from the nominal
level. A zero MCSE does not hide a deviation from nominal. The continuous
GRR and ICC statistics are monotone functions of the same variance ratio;
their percentile coverages coincide in these results. The integer-valued
ndc has discrete steps, which can produce conservative intervals and
overcoverage. The findings below identify every affected scenario and
interval estimand individually.

```{r coverage-tables, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
for (scenario in unique(coverage_results$data$scenario)) {
  cat("\n### ", scenario, "\n\n", sep = "")
  rows <- coverage_results$data[coverage_results$data$scenario == scenario, , drop = FALSE]
  names(rows)[names(rows) == "mcse"] <- "MCSE"
  performance <- rows[rows$estimand != "bootstrap", , drop = FALSE]
  print(knitr::kable(coverage_validation$latent_display(performance), row.names = FALSE))
  cat("\n\nBootstrap diagnostics:\n\n")
  print(knitr::kable(coverage_validation$latent_display(rows[rows$estimand == "bootstrap", , drop = FALSE]),
                     row.names = FALSE))
  cat("\n\n")
}
if (coverage_results$mode == "full") {
  findings <- m1d_validation$m1d_findings("boot_coverage", coverage_results$data, m1d_anchors)
  cat("\nReportable interval findings:\n\n")
  if (nrow(findings)) print(knitr::kable(m1d_validation$m1d_display(findings, digits = 6L), row.names = FALSE)) else
    cat("No interval estimand exceeds the anchored report threshold.\n")
} else cat("\nShort run: no full-run coverage finding is claimed.\n")
```
